event.title: Substack shuts down or files for bankruptcy
event.proposition: Substack shuts down its publishing platform or files for bankruptcy.
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of the definitive public announcement (company statement, court filing or SEC filing) that Substack has ceased operating its publishing platform or has filed for bankruptcy. A fall in writers, readers or revenue, a layoff, a down round, a leadership change or an acquisition that keeps the platform running does not count. Rumors and letters of intent do not count.

resolution_source.name: Substack company announcements; US bankruptcy court dockets via CourtListener

readings: 'will destroy this company' and the headline 'Will Destroy the Platform' are read as Substack ceasing to operate (shutdown or bankruptcy); decline without closure does not count.

records.stage_note: Substack is an operating private company on the statement date; the author reports no announced wind-down or bankruptcy.
records.note: Headline call of the post, addressed to Substack's CEO. No deadline words, so the item is undated (24-month window). The author publishes on Substack as a user; no disclosed role, stake or employment, so not affiliated. owen-0487 restates the same claim in the same post and is marked DUPLICATE (the first row stands).
Statement of intent about the author's own newsletter style; the author decides the outcome.

Title and preview restate the same claim as owen-0484 in the same post (Substack's moderation stance will destroy the platform). The first row (owen-0484) stands and carries the event new:substack-platform-shutdown. The finder hint on this row contains outcome information and was not used.
Own-newsletter content plan; the author decides whether and when to publish more about his father.
'Until we decriminalize those things' names no deciding body, jurisdiction, substance set or date, so no event can be written. The sentence is otherwise normative ('can and should be prosecuted').
'Change anything' in healthcare has no observable event, benchmark or resolution source. Entity (UnitedHealth Group) is named but the outcome is not. Satirical framing noted.
'Getting even bigger' is a comparative with no metric, threshold, series or period; present-tense characterization of the company's intent.
Statement of intent about the author's own newsletter content (satire of UnitedHealth Group).
'Drive us mad' is a metaphor with no observable event, entity or threshold. The subject (collective grief from overdose deaths) is also outside the five areas.
Overdose-death trend ('getting worse'); public-health epidemiology, not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice-adoption outcome. Present-tense trend statement with no threshold or period.
Expected worsening of abrupt overdose deaths from xylazine in the drug supply; public-health epidemiology outside the five areas. No series, threshold or period named.
Bereavement count derived from adolescent overdose deaths, 'more every year'; outside the five areas. The count is the author's own derived estimate, not a named public series.
'Drive us mad' is a metaphor with no observable event. Restates owen-0495 with a stronger phrase; same rejection.

The author states the FDA over-the-counter decision on Narcan as a present fact ('is now over the counter'), so the regulatory outcome was already public on the statement date. The remaining 'change that is coming' (retail availability) names no seller, series or date.
'A chance to save somebody's life' addressed to readers is not an observable event; no entity, series or threshold. 'Won't be long now' is not a deadline.
Own-newsletter content plan ('a story for later'); the author decides.

'That is on the verge of changing' does not say which rule or provision of inpatient psychiatric payment changes or how; the quote and its immediate context name only 'the 2024 CMS update'. An event cannot be written without invention. Teaser line ('Follow for More!'); 'on the verge' is not a deadline.
'I have been told they are coming' relays unnamed sources; the author neither endorses nor disputes the claim. Undated and without a named tool.
General pharmacological statement that antipsychotic augmentation causes weight gain; information about a known drug effect, not an expectation about a future event.
Rhetorical question in a footnote; 'GPT4 is going to do that' (drug naming) has no observable event, deciding body, series or resolution source.
Own-newsletter content plan ('That article is coming next'); the author decides. The implied claim that safer alternatives exist is not a forecast.
Slogan ('we are just getting started'); no entity decision, observable event or threshold.
'Highest hurdle' is a comparative with no resolvable benchmark: no series (for example NTAP denials by criterion), threshold or period is named.

Description of what the FY2024 proposed rule does (NTAP applies to inpatient psychiatric care in IPPS hospitals); information about a proposal's content, not an expectation that it is adopted. Magnus Medical's appended email disputes the description.

Slogans ('a revolution in ADHD for kids', 'Neuro-modulated future of our field'); no observable event, threshold, series or date. The author's practice Fermata offers the device (disclosed), which would make any device item affiliated.

Description of the current regulatory status of Monarch eTNS ('not yet cleared in Adults'); no expectation is stated. A future adult clearance would be decided by FDA on NeuroSigma's filing, so this is not CONTROL despite the Fermata disclosure.

The author labels the post 'pure clickbait' and 'Only satire'; 'a bazillion dollars' is hyperbole. The antecedent (somebody buys Calendly and offers a BAA) is not a defined event, so no conditional item can be written.
Author-labelled satire; 'Billions. Overnight success!' is hyperbole. The antecedent (somebody buys Zapier and allows a BAA) is not a defined event.
'Stay around' for fax machines and pagers names no metric, threshold, series or period; present-tense description of persistence.

Conditional 'the NTAP changes that if we leave comments': the antecedent (comments are filed) is under the author's control, as he runs the comment campaign and can comment himself, so the conditional rule rejects it as CONTROL. The consequent (CMS approves NTAP for SAINT) is coded from the author's own unconditional expectation at owen-0529. No lexicon phrase is present in the sentence.

'Could revolutionize our approach to mental health treatment' is a slogan with no observable event. The text is a GPT-4-drafted sample comment letter posted as a template, which also fails the own-words test.

'Democratize access' and 'improving the quality of life for countless individuals' have no observable event or threshold; the letter advocates for NTAP coverage rather than predicting it. GPT-4-drafted sample letter.

'It's obviously going to be a hospital' names no deciding body, product, series or resolution source; none of the eight templates fits a Vision Pro hospital use case. Inside a satirical open letter; 'obviously' is not a deadline.
Description of the proposed rule's effect ('has proposed CHANGES... that would allow Medicare to pay'); information about a proposal, not an expectation that CMS adopts it.
'This sets a precedent' has no observable event, benchmark or resolution source.
'They will need this payment model' states a need, not an observable event; no body decision, device set, series or threshold.

event.asset: SAINT Neuromodulation (Magnus Medical) Medicare new technology add-on payment
event.title: Medicare NTAP approved for SAINT Neuromodulation
event.proposition: CMS approves a Medicare New Technology Add-On Payment (NTAP) for SAINT Neuromodulation under the inpatient prospective payment system.
event.criterion: TRUE on the effective date of a Medicare inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) final rule, published in the Federal Register, that approves a New Technology Add-On Payment for SAINT Neuromodulation. The proposed rule, the open comment period, a coding assignment or a national coverage analysis is not approval.

resolution_source.name: Federal Register, CMS Medicare IPPS final rule (NTAP determinations)

readings: 'under Medicare, go to a hospital with depression and leave no longer depressed' is read as Medicare paying for SAINT in hospitals through the NTAP program the post names.
'79% of the time' restates the SAINT trial remission rate; it is not a separate scored claim.

records.stage_note: SAINT's NTAP application is on the FY2024 IPPS proposed-rule docket during the open comment period; CMS's determination is pending for the final rule. No base-rate class covers NTAP decisions.
records.note: Own-voice expectation (not the GPT-4 sample letter) that Medicare will pay for SAINT in hospitals via NTAP. 'In the near future' is not a deadline, so the item is undated (24-month window). 'could' sets bin C. Magnus Medical and SAINT are not in the author's affiliations, so not affiliated.
'The haters destroying the revolution all over again' is not an observable event; the rest is advice ('should stop trying to be the Blackberry') inside a satirical essay.
'A board complaint waiting to happen' names no medical board, clinician, jurisdiction, series or date.
Advice dressed as prediction; 'the only fun that matters will have a somber, defensible go-to-market strategy' has no observable event, benchmark or resolution source.
